sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Viviane, also known as Vivienne or Nimue, is an Arthurian heroine. She is the fairy beloved of the mighty wizard Merlin. In many accounts she is the same as Nimue, who some stories then link to the Lady of the Lake, champion of Arthur. Viviane is often credited with Merlin's magical end. Her reasons shift from tale to tale, from anger at his refusal to share his learning to jealousy of his straying affections, or a wish to spare him the sorrows of age. She sealed him within a tree trunk, or cast a charm that made him trust he was trapped inside it. That prison tree usually stands in the forest of Brocéliande in Brittany.

okr.objective: Present Viviane as the fairy lover of Merlin and a possible Lady of the Lake.
